title: Escrowed quota drip: smoothing daily/monthly resets with intermittent commit credits
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers on reserved capacity and metered plans report confusing immediate resets at daily/monthly boundaries (spiky invoices and sudden throttles) when usage events and late-arriving logs interleave across timezones. We propose an "escrowed quota drip" mechanism: instead of an instantaneous reset, move a bounded portion of next-period quota into an escrow bucket and release it (‘drip’) over a short warm-up window. This smooths spikes, simplifies reconciliations for late events, and reduces transient overage/negative-balance churn for reserved tenants.

Scope: implement escrow bucket + drip rate config per-tenant and per-plan, wire billing ledger adjustments, add reconciliation job for late events, and expose observability in Console (per-tenant escrow balance, drip rate, and reconciliation results). Ensure backward-compatible behavior and allow opt-out for customers who require hard resets.

Non-goals: changing long-term quota accounting semantics, replacing existing prorations for plan changes, or relaxing SLA guarantees for reserved pool throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable escrow bucket exists per tenant with size expressed as percent or absolute tokens
Drip window configurable (default 60s warm-up) and enforced by rate limiter before full quota availability
Billing ledger writes reflect escrow movements and reconciliation adjustments with immutable audit entries
Late events reconciliation job can backfill up to 7 days and produce deterministic ledger corrections and telemetry
Console shows escrow balance, current drip rate, and reconciliation history on tenant billing page
Opt-out toggle available for tenants; default enabled for new reserved capacity customers
Integration tests cover time-shifted events, DST and timezone boundary cases, and concurrent reset + reconciliation runs
No observable increase in median P50 token latency for hot routes (<3ms regression threshold) and percent of throttles due to resets reduced by >75% in test workload
